sentences.text: This review covers wellbore 15/9-F-15 in the Volve field, a development well in the Norwegian North Sea.
No data tools were available when this review was written, so it states no measured figures for depths, dates, hours, hole sizes or volumes.
Any quantitative statement about this wellbore should be taken from the field's daily drilling reports and checked against the source data before it is relied on.
The well was drilled in a sequence of hole sections, each opened below the casing shoe of the section above and closed by its own casing string.
For each section, the review should record the hole size, the start and end measured depth, the new hole drilled, and the casing shoe depth, using the values in the well data.
The section boundaries are the main reference points for judging drilling progress and for locating any hole problems that occurred during the well.
Activity time should be split into productive drilling and non-productive time, with the non-productive time grouped by cause and by hole section.
The primary lost-time causes should be read first, then the possible causes, so that the confirmed losses are not mixed with the uncertain ones.
Where lost time clusters in one section or one operation type, that cluster should be explained in the review rather than reported only as a total.
Drilling rate should be reviewed section by section, since rates in the softer near-surface formations and in the deeper sections are not comparable.
Rate changes should be linked to bit changes, mud changes and any reported tripping or reaming, so that the cause of each slowdown is identified.
Real-time curve statistics were not used in this review and are not reported here.
Before the review is issued, the figures should be filled in from the checked well data, and each one should be traced to its source report.
Lessons for future wells in the same field should focus on the sections and activities that caused the largest non-productive time, once those are confirmed from the data.
